clue.text: Having put on too much rouge appears embarrassed

definitions.text: Having put on too much rouge
definitions.meaning: literally, with cheeks coloured crimson by overdone make-up

explanation.definitionFit: Overdone blusher leaves a crimson complexion, and a blush of shame does the same, so the idiom covers both senses.

clue.text: Not the first print of children

parts.note: of in the sense 'concerning, about', which crosswords render as RE
issue is a legal and formal word for offspring

explanation.surface: A remark about a book's later printing that is somehow tied to children.
explanation.definitionFit: A second or later printing of a publication is a fresh release of something already published.

clue.text: Expert way to smear bridge player

parts.note: to dab is to apply paint or ointment with light pressing strokes
in bridge each of the four players, and the cards they hold, is called a hand

explanation.surface: An odd description of a card player, linked with the way someone spreads paint.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for someone highly skilled at a task, a real master of it.

clue.text: See modern fortress

parts.note: modern means new
a castle is a fortified stronghold

explanation.surface: An invitation to go and look at a newly built fort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a bishop's diocese. Newcastle is a cathedral city in north-east England and the seat of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a diocese, and the city on the Tyne in England is the seat of an Anglican bishop.

clue.text: The man had included work as expected

indicators.note: included signals that one piece is taken inside another here

parts.note: the man had contracts to he'd
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Some man had taken on a task, just as everyone foresaw.
explanation.definitionFit: To have wished for something is to have anticipated it with longing, as in 'it went as I'd anticipated'.

clue.text: Moved impatiently for the most part for ruffle

indicators.note: for the most part asks for nearly all of a word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to stalk off in an exaggerated, irritated way

explanation.surface: Someone fidgeting crossly most of the time over a frilly collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' cuts the final D from FLOUNCED.
explanation.definitionFit: A flounce is a gathered frill of fabric sewn onto a skirt or curtain, the same thing as a ruffle.

clue.text: Study steadfast support

parts.note: to con is to learn or study carefully
firm means steadfast, unwavering

explanation.surface: A careful look at reliable backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To corroborate a claim is to back it up, giving it support.

clue.text: Valuable boulder?

parts.note: read jokily, a big lump of rock that is worth a lot is a gem

explanation.definitionFit: A gem such as a diamond or ruby is a costly piece of rock, so 'valuable boulder' describes it playfully.

clue.text: How Sadie might compare notes?

parts.note: the name Sadie is the word ideas with its letters swapped around, so it is what you get by swapping them

explanation.surface: A suggestion of how a woman called Sadie might share information with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap round the letters of IDEAS and you get SADIE, so 'exchange ideas' describes how the name is formed.
explanation.definitionFit: To share thoughts and opinions with someone is to discuss what each has learned.

clue.text: Rear admiral in front of ship seen after shower

parts.note: RA is the naval abbreviation for Rear Admiral
the bow is the forward part of a vessel

explanation.surface: A senior naval officer standing at the prow, spotted once the rain has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc of colours appears in the sky when sunlight shines through raindrops after a downpour.

clue.text: It is said to rise anew from ashes in the capital

definitions.text: It is said to rise anew from ashes
definitions.meaning: the mythical bird reborn from its own funeral pyre

explanation.definitionFit: The legendary firebird is reborn from the embers of its pyre, and the same name belongs to Arizona's state capital.

clue.text: Accountant Virginia put Neddy in the plant

indicators.note: in signals that the donkey is placed inside the other letters

parts.note: CA is a Chartered Accountant
Neddy is a British pet name for a donkey
VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: An accountant called Virginia sticks a donkey among the shrubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neddy' is an informal British name for a donkey, so it gives ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Manioc is a tropical shrub whose starchy roots give tapioca, a staple crop plant.

clue.text: Scholarly Spaniard injured shin

parts.note: Don is the Spanish title for a gentleman, so a Spaniard

indicators.note: injured shows the letters of shin are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: A bookish man from Spain has hurt his lower leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a university teacher, bookish and academic in manner.

clue.text: In folklore a delectable mountain nymph

indicators.note: In tells the solver the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Folk tales tell of a charming spirit of the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is a nymph of the mountains, one of the hill spirits.

clue.text: Amber isn't bothered by one from the clan

indicators.note: bothered suggests the letters are upset and shaken into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman called Amber is not troubled by a member of the family group.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a tribe is someone belonging to a clan.

clue.text: Hopeless insider struggled round Pennsylvania

indicators.note: round means the scrambled letters go around the state abbreviation
struggled shows the letters of insider writhe into a new order

explanation.surface: An insider wrestled their way around an American state, with no hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hopeless' looks like it describes the insider, but it is the definition; the scrambled INDESIR from 'struggled' goes 'round' the state's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Without any hope at all, utterly despondent.

clue.text: Is this what toffee-maker eventually comes to?

definitions.text: Is this what toffee-maker eventually comes to?

parts.words: Is this what toffee-maker eventually comes to?
parts.note: read literally, a sweet-maker's finish would be gooey; the idiom means a bad death

explanation.definitionFit: A grisly or unpleasant demise, idiomatically, here punned on the gooey stickiness of toffee.

clue.text: Some swimmers entering take the plunge

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Several swimmers go into the pool and dive in.
explanation.definitionFit: To dunk oneself fully in water is to plunge into it.

clue.text: Viceroy, he had entered Kiev another way

indicators.note: entered means one piece goes inside the other
another way says the letters of Kiev are set out in a different order

parts.note: he had contracts to he'd

explanation.surface: A governor arrived in the Ukrainian capital by a different route.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiev is the older spelling of the Ukrainian capital; 'another way' rearranges it to KIVE, and 'entered' slips the contraction in after its first letter. A khedive governed Egypt for the Ottoman sultan.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Ottoman governor of Egypt, ruling as the sultan's deputy.

clue.text: Plotted line that surprisingly could be straight

definitions.text: Plotted line that surprisingly could be straight

parts.words: Plotted line that surprisingly could be straight
parts.note: on a graph, any plotted line is given this name even when it has no bend at all

explanation.definitionFit: In maths any line drawn on a graph is so called, including a perfectly straight one, despite the word suggesting a bend.

clue.text: Where in France central American led reindeer

indicators.note: led means the people go in front of the French word

parts.note: the Carib are an indigenous people of Central America and the Caribbean
ou is French for 'where'

explanation.surface: A guide from Central America took the lead with the reindeer somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led' is the charade order: the people come first. 'Where in France' asks for the French word, a common crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: The North American name for the reindeer of the Arctic tundra.

clue.text: Spiritual enlightenment about origin

parts.note: re means about, concerning
birth means origin, as in 'of noble birth'

explanation.surface: An account of spiritual awakening concerning where one came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Being born again in the spirit is a common image of religious awakening.

clue.text: The storm on stage

parts.note: a violent storm, and also the Shakespeare play of that name performed in the theatre

explanation.definitionFit: A violent gale is one sense, and Shakespeare's play about a shipwreck and a magician carries the name.

clue.text: Beat curtailed the plunder

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of the tail, so the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: to rob is to plunder

explanation.surface: The loot was trimmed down and beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse or rhythmic pounding, like a heartbeat.

clue.text: Wrote second edition copy to be included

indicators.note: to be included says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to crib is to copy someone else's work

explanation.surface: A second edition is being prepared with a copied passage added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be included' puts the copy inside the abbreviations; 'crib' as copying is schoolroom slang for cheating from another's work.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe or mark out letters is to have written, a rare literary sense.

clue.text: Northeast Republican contender more easily disturbed

parts.note: a vier is one who vies, a competitor

explanation.surface: A Republican candidate from the northeast is getting edgier.
explanation.definitionFit: More jumpy and anxious, quicker to be rattled.

clue.text: A former prince first in one of the provinces

indicators.note: first says the prince comes before the letter A

parts.note: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort

explanation.surface: A one-time royal leads the way in a region of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts ALBERT before A. The answer is a province of Canada, named after a daughter of Queen Victoria and Prince Albert.
explanation.definitionFit: A western Canadian province, one of that country's ten provinces.

clue.text: Simonstown now found in Cambridgeshire

parts.note: Simon is the apostle also called Peter
the town part of the word means a borough

explanation.surface: A South African naval town has somehow turned up in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Simonstown looks like the South African naval base, but read it as Simon's town: Simon Peter's borough. The city was once in Northamptonshire and is now in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral city is today within the English county of Cambridgeshire, after historic changes of county.
